title: Sortyard common definitions
description: Shared building blocks for every Sortyard domain object: identifiers, references, timestamps, content hashes, the tenancy field and the definition/state base shapes (design §3, §5.1). Not an object itself.

id.description: Stable identifier of an object. Opaque to clients.

ref.description: Reference to another object by its id.

versioned_ref.description: Reference to an immutable version of a definition (pinning, §5.1a).

version.description: Definition version label. Versions are immutable once materialised (§5.1).

content_hash.description: Content hash; definitions and context packets are content-addressed (§5.1c, §3.7a).

secret_ref.description: Pointer to a Secret object (secret.schema.json). Never a value (§3.7a).

actor.description: Who did something: a human operator, an agent (service account), the system, or a sensor.

scope.description: Where a policy or definition applies (§3.6).

absent_state.description: Named behaviour when the thing cannot run or its input is absent (§1.6; mandatory for eval gates).

object_base.description: Fields every workspace-scoped object carries. workspace_id exists from day one (§3.1).

definition_base.description: Definitions live in git and are materialised into the DB as immutable, content-hashed versions (§5.1).

source.description: Where the version was materialised from (§5.1: git mode or DB-only mode).
